https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Blanche defends DoJ’s pre-emptive suit to block Alaska Senate results certification
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Victoria Bekiempis
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
US attorney general calls CNN ‘crazy’ for suggesting Trump’s attempt to overturn election could lead to January 6 repeat

Todd Blanche, Donald Trump’s attorney general, lashed out during an interview on Sunday while defending the justice department’s pre-emptive lawsuit to block certification of Alaska’s US Senate results if the GOP incumbent loses, calling a TV host’s question “crazy”.

The testy repartee unfolded on CNN’s State of the Union over the DoJ’s unprecedented legal action, which alleges that there could be “voter confusion” due to two candidates named Dan Sullivan on Alaska’s ballot. Trump told reporters, “I’m the one that said do it” when asked about the suit.

Dana Bash, State of the Union host, said “one of the big questions is whether or not “Trump tries to overturn the election, and the result of that could be, God forbid, what we saw after January 6”.

“Oh, stop it,” Blanche said. “Oh, you got to stop it with that. You are not being a real person. Come on, man.

“I would have said that before January 6,” Bash said, referring to election-denying Trump supporters’ shocking attack on the Capitol. A bipartisan Senate report said there were seven deaths in relation to this incident.

“Because the president, because the Department of Justice, is concerned that there is an absolute fraud happening in Alaska, and he wants to do something about it, you’re saying, Mr Attorney General, because the president of the United States wants to stop a fraud and confusion in Alaska, is he going to do something crazy? That is not, that is not a real question.”

“We’re not laying any groundwork for the president to do that,” a fiery Blanche insisted. “What I said is the groundwork that we are laying is for Alaska, for the state of Alaska.”

“If it becomes an issue after the election, we’ll have the ability to determine whether there was confusion that violates the law in determining who the senators should be.”

Blanche also appeared irked during an interview with Margaret Brennan on CBS’s Face the Nation after she summed up the litigation and asked whether Trump directed him to file suit.

“Well first of all, let me correct you, OK,” Blanche said. “You described facts that were just simply either at best misleading, but really a lie to your viewers.”

While Trump’s DoJ has claimed there might be “voter confusion” on Alaskan ballots, potentially propelling Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola to victory, election experts maintain that this position is legally weak.

“The legal claim is so absurdly thin, there’s essentially no likelihood of success,” said Derek Mueller, a law professor at the University of Notre Dame, in a blogpost.

Another expert, David Becker, executive director of the Center for Election Innovation & Research, said this suit marked “an unprecedented intervention by the federal government” and noted that Alaska’s courts had “fully litigated” this issue.

The lawsuit, Becker said, “raises serious concerns about political interference” and that he could not remember “ever attempting to stop the certification of an election – and certainly not 11 days before polls close”.

Richard H Pildes, a law professor at New York University who focuses on elections, told the New York Times: “It is one of the weakest election lawsuits I’ve ever seen.”

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.title: NFL week seven: 49ers v Falcons, Colts v Vikings, Bengals v Ravens and more – updates
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.author: Graham Searles
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.text:
The speedy receiver catches the short throw then sprints through the heart of Cincy’s defense for a massive 48-yard touchdown. First blood Baltimore!

Minnesota go for it on 4th and 1 rather thank kicking a field goal and don’t get it!

Baltimore are across midfield already after a 16-yard catch for rookie tight end Josh Cuevas.

Here we go! Atlanta have kicked off and Brock Purdy and company will be on the field shortly as the 49ers looks to extend their perfect record to 7-0.

“Aaron Rodgers threw one touchdown pass and Chris Boswell kicked three field goals in Pittsburgh’s 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday in the NFL’s first regular-season game in France.

Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and scrambled for a key first down late in fourth quarter as the Steelers (5-2) won their third straight game.

Linebacker Payton Wilson had a red zone interception of Tyler Shough in the third quarter and the Saints (2-5) couldn’t recover. New Orleans rushed for just 18 yards.

With the Saints threatening on their opening drive of the second half, Wilson stepped in front of a short pass intended for Chris Olave. The Steelers got in field-goal position and Boswell was good from 39 yards for a 16-10 lead.

Patrick Queen sacked Shough on third down to stall a New Orleans with under seven minutes left in the fourth quarter.

Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and the interception.

Just before halftime, Rodgers was sacked by Carl Granderson on third down, and with 15 seconds left and no timeouts, the Steelers offense ran to the sideline. Boswell sprinted on and kicked a 47-yard field goal to give Pittsburgh a 13-10 lead at the half.

Rodgers’ 4-yard touchdown pass to 6-foot-7, 265-pound tight end Darnell Washington — with 5-foot-11 cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry in coverage — put the Steelers up 10-3.

Earlier on the drive, Rodgers moved in the pocket and found DK Metcalf for a 51-yard completion to the New Orleans 4. NFL France called it “quel caviar d’Aaron Rodgers.”

The Saints then tied it at 10-10 on Tyler Shough’s 1-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele on fourth-and-goal from the 1.” AP

Is second-year New Orleans head coach Kellen Moore on the hot seat? The Saints are 2-5 after a poor offensive display, they rushed for just 18 yards against the Steelers. Moore is 8-16 across his two seasons and finished last in the NFC South last year. They sit third at the moment but would be pushed into last place if Tampa Bay beat Carolina today. In a boost for the Buccaneers’ chances Baker Mayfield is back starting at quarterback after missing three games.

Speaking of divisional rivalries … today’s crunch matchup comes from the AFC North as the 3-2 Bengals face the 4-2 Ravens in Baltimore. Cincinnati will be happy Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson misses out again with an ankle injury as they aim to build on their best start since 2021 when they happened to make a visit to the Super Bowl. Baltimore are the underdogs then with Snoop Huntley at QB but if the Ravens get running back Derrick Henry going then all bets are off.

A win for either team is crucial in a congested division as the Pittsburgh Steelers have just moved top at 5-2 with a 16-10 win in Paris. The 4-2 Cleveland Browns are also gunning for top spot as they aim to keep a cracking start to the season going against the struggling 1-5 Tennessee Titans.

How about the NFL’s first encounter in France? It hasn’t been a vintage contest but the Steelers defense has won the day so far. With two minutes on the clock the 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers just rushed for a vital 1st down to get Pittsburgh in the red zone. New Orleans have two timeouts remaining trailing 16-10 and need a huge defensive play to have any hope of winning.

A likely win for the Steelers moves them to 5-2 and top of the AFC North at least until their divisional rivals all play in the next slate of games.

Bonjour football fans! Ça va? Bien! Welcome to week seven on the NFL with a distinctly French feel as Pittsburgh lead New Orleans 16-10 in Paris with only a couple of minutes remaining. While American football’s global takeover shows no signs of stopping, neither does the action as we have a treat in two unbeaten teams featuring in seven games starting at 12pm CST/1pm EST/5pm GMT (home teams listed second):

The pair of perfect franchises are the 49ers and Vikings who face the Falcons and Colts respectively. Minnesota’s mighty defense will be confident of making light work of an iffy Indianapolis offense but Atlanta have looked better than their record suggests this season and could give San Francisco a serious test.

Why might the 49ers be a little underpowered? Well, they are missing their biggest weapon in receiver Mike Evans who joins a lengthy list of injured wideouts. Tight end George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey will be called on to fill the void.

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Michael Carrick on the brink after Manchester United are humiliated by Bournemouth
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Jamie Jackson at Old Trafford
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
After Bruno Fernandes was dropped for “pure football” reasons – according to Michael Carrick – could Manchester United actually win a game of football?

The answer, again, was a resounding, humiliating no, and if the manager’s job remains in real peril, you have to wonder, too, if this beleaguered team should steel themselves for a relegation dogfight. They lack imagination, cohesion, fight, confidence and anything resembling joy, and so, now they hover a point above the drop zone, survival cannot be taken for granted.

Goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson downed United this afternoon yet what has killed Carrick and side in the past fortnight is the insubordination of Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez plus the deeper malaise of a club that is riven by factions.

The Sir Jim Ratcliffe-led football department may issue Carrick the bullet but the next man – Eddie Howe is favoured and is open to the job – will surely not break the boom-bust cycle that is each new manager’s fate. Before this latest debacle, you had to flick the calendar back 45 days to 10 September (eight games ago), for the last time United chalked up a “W” and gave their fans reason to cheer.

Once more Carrick’s men failed to do so. Equally as disappointing is how, in the days since Fernandes’s public takedown of Carrick, no apology has been forthcoming from the captain.

Where Martínez did say sorry for criticising Jason Wilcox (though, not to the director of football), the United captain’s silence speaks volumes. If Carrick made an error in not dropping Martínez for his outburst, discarding Fernandes was the correct call and so Harry Maguire’s redemption arc was complete, being handed the armband, after it was taken off him and given to the Portuguese in July 2023.

Now, Carrick surely fears being removed after a buoyant Bournemouth made it four successive wins versus an opponent offering scant resistance, as the boos ringing out at the end signified.

As is the case for this Carrick iteration, midfield control was an issue throughout. Youri Tielemans lost the ball, Bournemouth’s passing went tap-tap-tap, and United were turned.

Even when Leny Yoro fashioned a one-two with Tielemans and swept the ball left to Diogo Dalot, the move foundered, and moments later the young right-back was clearing from beneath his bar as a Rayan cross went close to teeing Evanilson up. All of this, yet again, pointed to a team that seem unable to execute whatever Carrick’s plan is.

Senne Lammens would hoof upfield aimlessly, Maguire would head possession back to a white shirt instead of chesting down, and as the half hour passed a wild Dalot shot was their sole one registered.

When Bournemouth scored it was due to United shooting themselves in both feet. First came Ayden Heaven’s wild scissor challenge that had Evanilson leaping out of danger and was adjudged a yellow-card offence.

The second self-inflicted moment came when Justin Kluivert’s free-kick, on a diagonal from Bournemouth’s right, was allowed to drop on Rayan’s boot freely with the Brazilian entirely unmarked.

“Sacked in the mornin cog” came the derisory chants from the travelling faithful and when their men doubled their lead on 42 minutes you wondered if Carrick might not last until then.

Again, this should have been avoided. This time Yoro was to blame as he contrived to slip near United’s area, allowing Adrien Truffert to collect; the left-back squared to Tavernier, who slid into the net.

Cue the unfurling of a Stretford End tifo that said: “STANDARDS” above the faces of Eric Cantona, Bryan Robson and Roy Keane, the Cherries congregation this time offering, “going down with the City”, on repeat.

Carrick’s move for a second half that might decide his fate was to take off Tielemans for Matheus Cunha, Mason Mount (anonymous again), taking the No 10 position. If the manager had, indeed, dropped Fernandes for his form, then the opening period was a fair argument to reinstate him. Yet if Rayan had not fluffed a simple chance to make it 3-0 – the attempt was a pea-roller – even the mutineer would not be able to save United.

Next, though, it was game – and possibly Carrick’s tenure – over. Lammens charged out to clear a through ball, Evanilson beat him to it, rounded the flailing No 1, and from around 40 yards out on the right sliced a curving finish into the waiting net.

Carrick’s visage was a picture of hurt. On the bench, Fernandes zipped his top right up, while in his posh seat, Wilcox sank lower into his winter coat. This would not stop him hearing, towards the end, abusive chants directed towards him. They were cruel, but there is true pain being felt in these parts.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.title: Exiled opposition leader María Corina Machado returns to Venezuela
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text:
Nobel peace prize winner’s return after almost a year in exile is unlikely to please interim president Delcy Rodríguez

The Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has announced she has returned to Venezuela almost a year after she left the country to receive the Nobel peace prize.

Her close ally Edmundo González, who is in exile, confirmed her arrival. “Venezuela! I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil,” he posted on social media. “Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” he said, adding that he too would soon return.

It was not immediately clear how Machado, 59, had managed to return to Venezuela but footage on social media showed she was in Barquisimeto, the capital of Lara state, which is about 220 miles west of the capital, Caracas.

Images showed her surrounded by supporters holding mobile phones in a church called the Sanctuary of the Divine Shepherdess.

The Trump administration had reportedly opposed Machado’s return, believing her presence would complicate the cosy relationship it has struck up with the interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, since abducting her former boss, Nicolás Maduro, in January.

Machado slipped out of Venezuela last December – a few weeks before Maduro’s capture – and in recent months has reportedly made more than half a dozen failed attempts to return home, including after the devastating earthquake that hit the northern coast in June.

After Maduro was seized, many had expected Donald Trump to give Machado his blessing to take power. Her movement is widely believed to have beaten Maduro in the 2024 presidential election, but he refused to hand over power.

Instead the US president embraced Rodríguez, Maduro’s vice-president, who now governs a country widely seen as a US protectorate.

Machado has repeatedly heaped praise on Trump for launching the operation to remove Maduro, and gave him her 2025 Nobel peace prize medal, which she had been awared for her peaceful challenge to Venezuela’s authoritarian government.

Asked by reporters on Sunday about her return, Trump said: “I don’t know anything about it, but I think she’s a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel prize, so how can I say anything else?”

“I hope she’s safe. She’s a very nice woman. But we’re doing very well in Venezuela,” he said.

https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oc.title: ‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’: Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron Cohen
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oc.author: Catherine Shoard
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oc.text:
Exclusive: Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’

Joshua Loudermilk, one of two men apparently discredited by the new Ali G movie Ali G: Who Iz I?, has said that he was in on the joke, but that the film-makers didn’t realise this.

Loudermilk, a 54-year-old aspiring actor from North Carolina, has told the Guardian he recognised star Sacha Baron Cohen early in the shoot but continued pretending to be a hard-right Maga sympathiser prepared to defend the US border at all costs.

The movie involves Loudermilk being recruited by another Cohen character, the ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad, to help form a citizens’ warrior force to protect US borders, making use of his top-secret new weapon: a gun disguised as buttocks.

Along with fellow recruit Michael Aboud, the chair of the El Paso county Republican party, Loudermilk joins Morad on a mission to stop the birth on US soil of the baby of a fictional South American drugs kinpin. This involves abducting a woman apparently in labour, abandoning her in a deserted medical facility, kidnapping her newborn child (a lifelike prosthetic) and driving it in a zipped bag to the border in order to deliver it by drone to Mexico.

Aboud is shown taking the decision to drop the child from a great height into Mexico rather than have it touch US soil. He has since called Cohen a “liar” and a “pervert” and expressed his intention to sue. The film repeatedly stresses that both men were “not in on it”.

Loudermilk has told the Guardian he was surprised the production company did not notice social media updates he posted shortly after the shoot in which he named Cohen and expressed his excitement about the project.

But rather than being upset about his involvement, Loudermilk – who recently appeared as Squire Dap in the North Carolina Town of Hudson Fall Dinner Theatre’s production of Camelot – says he welcomes the publicity boost.

“I want to use this to my benefit,” he says. “I would hope Sacha would read this and laugh, like: ‘Hey, you got me!’ I had so much fun creating that character. I was trying to see if I was any good at acting in comedy. And I realised: ‘Oh, I think I’m good at this.’ And that’s what I wanna do for the rest of my life.”

His experience began in September 2025 when Loudermilk spotted a post on Craigslist by a body called the American Citizen Initiative (whose website is no longer active) recruiting “patriotic legal Americans” “concerned about the border crisis” who “believe that illegal immigration is out of control”.

The ad, one of dozens posted across US states simultaneously, invited “real American citizens” to “attend an exclusive, hands-on event experience where you’ll learn the truth about what’s happening on the border and how you can make a difference”. Attendees were promised $300 as well as travel expenses.

“I was like: this seems kind of weird,” says Loudermilk, who describes himself as broadly apolitical. “I don’t really care much about our borders. My mom’s from Ireland.”

Recently made redundant, his motivation for responding was primarily financial. “I know rightwing and leftwing organisations have money and will pay people to just hold a sign up. I remember thinking: I wanna get on that gravy train. I want some George Soros money. I’ll pretend to be whatever. Just let me feed my family. It could have been save the whales and I would have done it.”

In his application, Loudermilk fabricated hard-right views, mentioned that he had been a preacher and neglected to declare his ambitions to become a comedy actor – in part, he says, out of embarrassment. He then filled in a “silly questionnaire – very obvious, very slanted to the right”.

Loudermilk was then called for a video interview, which involved the identification of left-leaning celebrities, as well as figures including Borat, Cohen’s bumbling Kazakh reporter, who Loudermilk duly named.

He was also asked if he was a Trump supporter. “The funny thing is: not really. He’s just a leader. But I was like: I’m going to be an improv actor so I said: ‘Yeah, I support Trump!’ Next thing I know they’re like, ‘We want you to come out to be a part of this.’

The company flew him to Ontario, California, with an initial offer of $1,000, plus food and expenses, on top of which Loudermilk received a further $700. “It was all real secretive. They frisked me down and I got in a truck to go to a karate studio.”

Once he arrived, Loudermilk was greeted by security and informed an Israeli commander wanted to meet him. “That was a red flag. Why would Israeli commander be in America? I go in there and immediately I see this really tall guy with this horrible plastic surgery. My first thought was: that looks like Sacha Cohen. But I was like: nah, that can’t be him.”

Loudermilk’s suspicions were further raised, he says, when he met his fellow recruits. “They were old, old, old white guys who were really out of shape. Everyone’s wearing these Trump shirts. They didn’t seem like warriors. I thought: they could probably get better people for this.”

Morad then produced the top-secret new gun in the shape of large, strap-on bottom, out of which bullets are fired from the anus. Initially, Loudermilk was baffled by its logistics. “I kept thinking: no-one’s gonna wear that thing because your butt’s gonna be abnormally large. No one has a butt like that. Are you gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that. And you’d have to wear some really big khaki pants.”

He volunteered to be first to try the weapon out, whereupon Morad demonstrated the trigger system, which involves the pumping of an attached rubber penis. “And he kept calling it ‘shmeckel’. I’m like: that’s Sacha Cohen. At that moment I knew it.

“And I was like: oh no, I can’t break character. I’ve got to go along with it. So what I decided [was] that whatever he did, I was going to take it another step further. He’s not going to punk me; I’m going to trick him. So I decided to get into character and just have a good time because they’re paying me.”

As the plot became more “ridiculous”, says Loudermilk, so his enjoyment increased. During a scene in which he, Morad and Aboud help deliver the (prosthetic) baby, the three men become covered with fake excrement. “This big blast of pooping pap,” recalls Loudermilk – but he was reassured after inadvertently sampling some of the fluids. “I thought: ‘This doesn’t taste bad.’ So I just kind of hung in there. It was disgusting, but I was having fun.”

At the climax at the Mexican border, says Loudermilk, he handed the remote control to the drone to Aboud, “because that was boring. It was ridiculous – they’re not flying a real baby”. Instead, he “wanted to have fun with Sacha,” so he grabbed the “butt-gun”, yelling about the need to defend themselves, and eventually discharged fire, aided by Morad, who helps pump the penis trigger.

Loudermilk declines to defend Aboud’s decision to then endanger the life of the baby by dropping it from the drone, but expresses some sympathy for his unwitting co-star.

“I felt sorry for the poor fella. Because I’m all-in and he’s just kind of following me around like in a daze, like: what’s happening? He was scared to death, and obviously very uncomfortable, bless his heart.

“I’d never met the guy before, but [at times] it felt he was totally freaking out on me. So I had to make him believe that I believed all this. So I would tell him, ‘You’re being a wimp, man. Our freedom is on the line.’ I kept trying to keep him from quitting.

“But I’m surprised he didn’t figure it out. Like, come on, Michael – why would they recruit you to defend our border? Think about it.”

Loudermilk concedes his decision to maintain the pretence of being far-right once he had worked out the true nature of the project was in part because he “was a little offended. Like: really? You’re picking on these Americans that aren’t the brightest. You’re gonna make fun of them and they’re not gonna know any better. So I decided I needed to be their ally, even though I’m not that way.”

At the end of filming, Loudermilk signed a non-disclosure agreement at the request of the production company, which he says he was not given a copy of, and which mostly related to the top-secret weapons. “They came up to me after I was done and said, ‘Oh, you did so well!’ I said, ‘You get what you need? Can I talk about it?’ They said, ‘Oh no, not yet. Especially the butt-gun.’”

Loudermilk considers any such terms breached now the film is out and mentions him by name: “It’s fair game.” He adds that, after shooting, he had some qualms about not coming clean to them that he had twigged. “I felt a little bad. And that’s why I thought: I should make a little post.”

In December last year, Loudermilk posted three times on his public Facebook page about “eight hours of intense filming one on one with Sasha [sic] Cohen”, as well as twice on his Instagram, which is also public.

“But they never saw it. And the fact they missed that makes it even better to me. So I guess it’s on them.”

Last week, representatives for the film confirmed again to the Guardian that Loudermilk was not in on the joke. They have not yet responded to a further followup question on this.

The film was released nationwide in the UK on Friday, as well as in a limited run in the US. Loudermilk, who has not yet watched it, says he is unconcerned about the prospect of recriminations from anyone upset by his apparent actions.

“That people would be disgusted is a compliment. Oh, I really did a good job, huh! I pulled it off and I was so proud of myself.”

https://www.theguardian.com/world/ng-int.title: This comedian jokes about deportation … but it is happening for real
https://www.theguardian.com/world/ng-int.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent; photographs by Clodagh Kilcoyne
https://www.theguardian.com/world/ng-int.text:
Despite job offers, Jaishree Malik has had visa renewal and extension requests delayed and denied, and she is not alone

Jaishree Malik bounds on to the Cheeky Monkey comedy club stage and brandishes an envelope – it is a letter from the Irish government. Would the audience like to hear what’s in the letter?

“Yeah,” the first rows reply. She repeats the question, prompting a louder response. “Yeah!”

Malik extracts typed A4 pages and begins to read. “I wish to advise you that under section 3 of the immigration act 1999, the minister for justice, home affairs and migration is proposing to make a deportation order in your case.”

A nervous laugh ripples across the audience, then there’s a pause. “Oh,” says someone.

Malik beams. “Don’t worry, it’s not for you.” She resumes reading. “The reason for this is because you have remained in the state without permission […] you are therefore a person whose deportation would, in the minister’s opinion, be conducive to the common good.”

For the audience in the basement of the International bar in central Dublin, the penny drops: the letter is real. Malik, 25, is facing deportation to her native India.

“Did you know you were friends with a criminal?” she asks. “I’m sorry you had to find out this way.” She cracks a few more jokes, then: “In case you can’t tell, I’m fucking furious about this.” She concludes her set to whoops and applause.

Malik is not being deported - she is leaving voluntarily - but she may be the only immigrant to turn her deportation order into comedy. Plenty of others share her anger at a system they say has become harsh and arbitrary.

The Irish government has toughened border enforcement and rules on migration, asylum and naturalisation amid a housing shortage and strain on public services partly attributed to immigration. Placards at anti-immigration protests declare that “Ireland is full”.

The justice minister, Jim O’Callaghan, has said the authorities wish to curb population growth that is seven times the EU average. Critics say the welcome mat has been withdrawn unfairly from deserving cases, including students from Gaza denied visas despite scholarship offers from Irish universities.

Others, such as Malik, have had visa renewal and extension requests delayed and denied despite job offers. “It’s Kafkaesque. Why would I read The Trial? I’m living it,” she said in an interview, referencing the novel about a protagonist pitted against unreasoning bureaucracy.

From Gurgaon, near Dehli, Malik moved to Ireland in 2022 on a student visa to pursue an M.Phil (Master of Philosophy) in literature at Trinity College Dublin. She had a job on campus during her studies advising prospective and current students. After graduating she obtained a visa that let her stay and work for two years through the Third Level Graduate Scheme and continued working at Trinity with international exchange students.

She moved to another job in Trinity and applied to the department of justice to extend her visa, pending confirmation of a new one, but a delay in processing the application led to Malik losing that job in February and entering legal limbo. The department told her she had no right to work while the application was being processed.

She submitted additional information to bolster her case and, while awaiting a ruling, subsisted on savings and channelled her anxiety at open mic comedy nights. Malik had dabbled in comedy at Trinity but never previously performed around the city.

“Your best material comes when your life is falling apart. But the first time I was so scared. I was reading bits from my phone. It wasn’t landing very well, I didn’t know where to pause. But I got a lot of good feedback. All the comedians were absolutely lovely.”

Malik refined her act and incorporated her exasperation when the department of public works offered a job that she could not accept because of the visa imbroglio. “It’s so absurd. I’m being offered a job by the government that I can’t take because of the government.”

Some audiences think she is playing a character, she said. “They come up to me and say, ‘Oh, that’s so funny’. Then I explain and they’re like, ‘Oh wait, it’s actually real?’”

Ivana Bacik, a legislator and leader of the Labour party, said Malik’s case reflected a hardening of immigration policy. “It’s impacting on lots of people and indeed lots of employers because they’re losing good people.”

The department of justice was using “spurious reasons” to deny visas to Gaza students, said Bacik. “I believe there’s much more compassion and warmth towards inward migration among Irish communities and it’s not reflected in the ministry’s approach.”

A group that represents the Gaza students said the “breakdown” started this summer. “We were refused for documents we were never asked to provide, such as a bank statement and proof of intention to return,” it said in an emailed statement. “We were then told to appeal with original documents by post, and as you know, Gaza is destroyed and there is no postal service.” The students have taken test cases to Ireland’s high court.

A department of justice spokesperson said he could not comment on the court cases but that screening and verification were integral to the immigration system and that there had been no change in policy towards Palestinian students. “Each visa application is assessed on its own merits.”

For Malik, the battle to remain in Ireland ended with the deportation letter sent on 5 October. She will leave next month but continue performing until the end.

“I am very angry but when I get up on stage and I make people laugh, it sort of disarms the anger and the political stuff. If I can go up there and make you laugh about something so powerful it makes it less powerful and it becomes the joke. That is the jester’s privilege.”

Ireland is not immune to xenophobia and racism but audiences have been supportive, said Malik. “I’m talking about visas, yes, but under this I am still a person. I’ve made a lot of Irish friends who are basically family and they’re all outraged on my behalf.”

She has not fully absorbed the fact she must leave, she said. “I don’t think it’ll hit me until I’m on the plane.” She is bracing for “reverse culture shock” once back in India.

In the meantime, Malik is preparing to shed her possessions, close her bank account and pack before heading in the early hours of 14 November to Dublin airport. “My flatmate drives and she’s offered to take me even though it’s a very inconvenient time. That’s a very good flatmate. Shout out to the flatmate.”

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Andy Hunter at Anfield
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile.

There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break.

Fabian Hürzeler praised the Brighton performance and the self-belief necessary to take the game to Liverpool when trailing to two quick-fire goals. But he exaggerated the threat they displayed. Yasin Ayari missed a glorious chance to open the scoring and also struck a post, but Alisson was troubled more by his own distribution after Liverpool’s second goal than by anything the visitors engineered.

“I think everyone in the stadium saw there was one team who really tried to create and tried to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,” claimed the Brighton head coach, prompting a mass raising of eye-brows in the post-match press conference. “The difference was that they scored and we didn’t. They blocked a lot of shots and defended the box well. We didn’t have that efficiency. We couldn’t keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes and lost some important personal duels but overall I saw a team with a lot of good things. It is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.”

Storm Boelo raged outside the stadium but inside it was relatively calm, vindicating the decision to proceed with the game. But not for Brighton. Liverpool’s attacking force devastated the visitors’ hopes of a fifth straight win and clean sheet in succession in the Premier League. The hosts were aggressive and sharp from the start, in contrast to their opening against Villarreal in the Champions League, and opened the scoring just as Brighton were beginning to exert their first serious spell of pressure.

There was an element of good fortune about the breakthrough but it also encapsulated the differing intensity between the teams when Wirtz held off Lewis Dunk and Araújo beat both the Brighton captain and Oliver Boscagli to the loose ball. His low cross pin-balled off two Brighton players before rebounding to Wirtz, whose first time shot deceived Bart Verbruggen via another deflection off Gross. Wirtz’s low key celebration hinted at what was to come. It was not his first league goal of the campaign and second goal in successive games after all. The breakthrough was officially credited as an own goal from the Brighton midfielder.

It should also have been a Liverpool equaliser rather than the opener. Diego Gómez and Gross combined to pierce Liverpool’s left flank and present Ayari with a free sight of goal with Alisson dragged across to his left. The Brighton forward blazed high into the Kop and would soon have added reason to rue the miscue.

Liverpool soon doubled their lead when capitalising on more casual Brighton defending. Boscagli was again found wanting when attempting to deal with Alisson’s clearance. The left-back struck a clearance straight at Barcola and was left floundering as the France international, deployed on the right, brushed aside his efforts to recover possession. Isak steered Barcola’s delivery inside the far corner with a deft, side-foot finish to score in three consecutive league games for the first time since January 2025. There was no surprise whatsoever when Boscagli was withdrawn at half-time.

Brighton attacked with greater conviction than they defended but with Araújo, Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk making telling interventions, and receiving impressive support from all quarters, Alisson was not seriously extended. The visitors’ best hope of a recovery stemmed from the Liverpool keeper’s own risky pass to Alexis Mac Allister, which gifted possession back to Brighton and resulted in Ayari striking a post from 20 yards out.

Jack Hinshelwood, Boscagli’s replacement, and fellow substitute Malick Yalcouyé injected more energy and bite into Brighton’s second-half display but an end product from the visitors remained lacking. Too many overhit crosses and poor final balls enabled Liverpool to protect their lead in comfort.

Iraola said: “It is a very valuable win. The key was how we started. We needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions, and we’ve done it and it has been a different game from the last ones when we’ve conceded first.”

https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2.title: Brazil runoff live updates: polls set to close as Flávio Bolsonaro narrowly leads Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in race for presidency
https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2.author: Marina Dunbar
https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2.text:
Sunday’s election is a test for incumbent Lula: can he can rally enough support to overturn Bolsonaro’s lead?

Thundering to a crowd of thousands of far-right supporters in São Paulo on 7 September, Brazil’s Independence Day, the senator Flávio Bolsonaro focused less on his opponent in the presidential election, the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, than on someone who is not running at all.

“Whoever votes for Lula is voting for Alexandre de Moraes,” Bolsonaro shouted, referring to the shaven-headed supreme court justice once described as “Voldemort” by Elon Musk.

Although Lula did not appoint Moraes to the court, Bolsonaro’s supporters have linked the two men ever since the judge oversaw the case in which the senator’s father, the former president Jair Bolsonaro, was sentenced to 27 years in prison for attempting a coup.

Just days before the election runoff, Moraes was once again at the centre of a presidential scandal – one that Lula believes may have helped Flávio Bolsonaro overtake him to emerge as the frontrunner. The justice once hailed as democracy’s “saviour” for containing Jair Bolsonaro may now have helped pave the way for the family’s return to power.

The scandal began with a police investigation, which found that Moraes’s wife’s law firm had a contract worth about £20m with Daniel Vorcaro, the banker accused of orchestrating Brazil’s largest banking fraud. Text messages also emerged suggesting a close relationship between Moraes and Vorcaro, though the judge denies the messages are authentic.

Investigations subsequently revealed that at least four other justices had links to the disgraced banker, meaning half of the court’s 10 current justices have been drawn into the scandal.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Brazilian presidential runoff.

Leftwing president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and senator Flávio Bolsonaro faced a second round of voting after neither secured more than 50 per cent of the vote in the first round.

Bolsonaro, the eldest son of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, pulled off a surprise first-round victory, signaling a resurgence of the far-right in Brazil. But polls appeared to have narrowed a few days before Sunday’s vote, with a Quaest poll reported by Reuters showing Bolsonaro on 45% of the vote, with Lula on 44%. A week earlier, Bolsonaro had 46% of the vote, compared to Lula’s 44%.

In the first-round election earlier this month, Bolsonaro secured 47% of the vote, compared with Lula’s 45%.

Sunday’s election is a test for incumbent president Lula: can he can rally enough support to overturn Bolsonaro’s lead?

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: US south-west braces for more storms after enduring days of rain and flooding
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Coral Murphy Marcos and agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
More inclement weather forecast in rain-soaked Four Corners region after evacuations and rescues last week

Another round of heavy showers and thunderstorms were expected to hit the south-west US on Sunday after the region endured days of rain that forced evacuations, water rescues and multi-million-dollar damage.

The National Weather Service issued a flood watch for much of the Four Corners – the meeting point of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah – even as local officials forecast further receding of swollen rivers that surged since rains picked up on Wednesday.

About 4ft (1 meter) of water flooded the home of Shane Ferrari, the sheriff of San Juan county, New Mexico. He said the area’s situation was stable on Sunday, but he and other residents were trying to clean up and deal with damage.

The New Mexico governor, Michelle Lujan Grisham, said in a statement on Saturday that law enforcement had reported hundreds of water rescues between the cities of Farmington and Bloomfield.

“Families in Bloomfield and Farmington spent the night on rooftops watching the river flood their homes, and our national guard and state police crews have been bringing them to safety,” said Lujan Grisham. “Right now, our focus is saving lives. If you’re told to evacuate, go. Once the water recedes, the state will do everything in its power to help San Juan county families rebuild.”

The San Juan River in Farmington on Friday ran 2 ft above its previous record set in 1909.

San Juan county spokesperson Devin Neeley said the county did not have official numbers on damage to homes or the number of people evacuated, but he was not aware of any loss of life.

Neeley said the flood waters were receding but left mud and silt, much of which has been contaminated with sewage because of failures at waste plants. There were still power outages affecting multiple areas, and it would probably be a few days until residents got their power back on.

“It’s a pretty active disaster zone,” he said. “We’re not on the downswing by any means.”

The flooding is just the latest from two months of on-and-off heavy rain caused by tropical moisture coming ashore from the Pacific. After months of drought, other recent deadly flooding struck the Grand Canyon and areas of New Mexico.

On the US broadcast, Apple has decided to bring on as its expert … Apple CEO John Ternus. We find out that he likes driving and thinks F1 (broadcast on Apple TV) is growing rapidly in the US and he think F1 The Movie (produced by Apple Studios) was very good. Funny that.

Who says nice guys don’t finish first? Kimi may well not clinch the title today, but he almost certainly will soon. Giles Richards looked at why Everyone Loves Kimi for us earlier this week:

So here we are. Nine-year-old Kimi Antonelli* has a chance to become the youngest champion in F1 history today – and he’s sitting on pole too. He leads the championship by 102 points over his Mercedes teammate George Russell. He’ll clinch the championship if he wins and Russell finishes outside the top eight, with Lewis Hamilton outside the top four. While the two Britons will push Antonelli, the man who appears to be most on his mind is Max Verstappen, who has been in brilliant form – and not just against amateur karters – and sits second on the grid in Austin.

“Max has been very quick and did an incredible job in qualifying so it’s not going to be easy,” Antonelli said on Saturday. “Hopefully we’ll be leading into turn one and we’ll try to set the pace, even though it’s going to be very tight.”

https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.title: Barcelona v Real Madrid: El Clásico – live
https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.author: Niall McVeigh
https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.text:
Barcelona (4-2-3-1): Joan García; João Cancelo, Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín, Xavi Espart; Rodri, Pedri; Lamine Yamal, Fermín López, Gordon; Raphinha.

Subs: Szczesny, Livakovic, Balde, Fariñas, Gavi, De Jong, Bernal, Adeyemi, Abdelkarim, Campos, Goren.

Real Madrid (4-2-3-1): Lunin; Valverde (c), Konaté, Huijsen, Cucurella; Tchouameni, Bernardo Silva; Diomande, Bellingham, Arda Güler; Mbappé.

Subs: Mestre, Illia, Militão, Camavinga, Endrick, Alexander-Arnold, Carreras, Espí, Brahim Díaz, Rüdiger, Dumfries, Thiago.

Tonight’s game also takes place against a weekend of unrest in Barcelona. There were 128 arrests overnight for acts of “vandalism, damage to public property and looting” in the city centre, according to the regional Catalan police.

The match is still going ahead, with an increased security presence already in place after the game was deemed “high-risk” by police last week. Back in 2019, this fixture was postponed due to protests in Barcelona.

We’ll have full team news shortly, but Real Madrid keeper Thibaut Courtois has already been ruled out of tonight’s game due to illness. “Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal (from the squad) due to a bout of the flu,” Madrid said in a statement. The Ukrainian goalkeeper Andriy Lunin is set to step in for Mourinho’s side.

Is the clásico making a comeback? A bitter rivalry that has raged for more than a century, Barcelona v Real Madrid may have been the world’s biggest sporting fixture during the era of Ronaldo and Messi, Mourinho and Guardiola. Incredibly skilful players dragged into extraordinarily spiteful on-pitch battles, each game felt like a heavyweight title fight.

These two teams remain the dominant forces in Spain, and their mutual hatred of one another is still very much intact. Still, the clásico has lost some of its intensity in recent years – but there are signs it may be coming back. Chief among those signs is Mourinho’s dramatic return to Real Madrid, where he is rebuilding the media war that wore both coaches out at the end of the rivalry’s unmissable age.

There is also, crucially, a touch of jeopardy about tonight’s game, particularly for the visitors. Hansi Flick’s Barcelona have started the league season with nine straight wins and are six points ahead of Madrid; that gap could be nine points, or three points, after tonight’s events at Camp Nou. The outcome may depend on Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé, two exceptional players poised to dominate this derby for the next decade.

In short, the biggest game in world football is back. Kick-off is at 8pm GMT, 9pm local time, so get comfortable.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Anthropic sued for allegedly using 274 Elvis Presley songs to train AI models
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Marina Dunbar
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Authentic Brands Group says AI company infringed on rights of songs by the King such as Can’t Help Falling in Love

The owners of Elvis Presley’s music catalogue are suing artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic for allegedly using Presley’s songs to train their models without permission.

Authentic Brands Group, the licensing organization that has ownership of both Presley’s music and likeness, is accusing Anthropic of infringing on the rights of 274 songs by Presley. The lawsuit, first reported by Billboard, was filed on Friday.

While AI firms have already faced copyright infringement claims from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) and music labels such as Sony, Universal and Warner Records, this case represents one of the first major legal challenges brought directly by an artist’s estate against an AI developer. The result could set a broader precedent for how AI companies are allowed to use existing music catalogues.

“The Elvis plaintiffs bring this action to enforce these exclusive rights against the defendant that has built its entire business model based on copyright infringement at a scale never seen before,” lead attorney Richard Busch wrote in the lawsuit.

The lawsuit claims that “from its inception, Anthropic’s AI model, ‘Claude,’ has created infringing output of copyrighted material of virtually every song from every catalog available on the internet”.

It further accuses Anthropic of utilizing 274 of Presley’s songs to train its AI model. These works include Can’t Help Falling in Love, All Shook Up and A Little Less Conversation. The plaintiffs are seeking $150,000 per infringed track, or about $41m (about £31m).

“Even Anthropic’s institution of guardrails (albeit ineffectively) to purportedly limit outputs which infringe upon music copyrights, after being caught, along with its knowledge that its guardrails were ineffective to stop creating outputs which infringed music copyrights, demonstrates that Anthropic knowingly engaged and continues to willfully engage in copyright infringement of others’ musical works,” the lawsuit states.

AI music platforms work by analyzing large amounts of recorded music in order to learn the sounds, structures and expressions of songs, and then allows users to create their own AI-generated music via text or speech prompts.

Musicians have repeatedly expressed concerns that their music and voices are being used without their permission by AI models, as well as fears that AI-generated “slop” music could replace human-made songs.

Some AI bots have even begun impersonating real living artists on music streaming platforms. Last week, music streaming giant Spotify announced it had removed about 50m songs considered AI slop from its recommendations to users over the past year.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.title: Macron’s ‘vandals pay’ bill puts right to protest at risk
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text:
Making innocent protesters liable for damage would be bad for rule of law and play into far-right hands, say opponents

Emmanuel Macron has been accused by trade unions of trying to curb the fundamental French right to protest as the government fast-tracks a bill to make protesters pay for damage caused by vandalism at street demonstrations even if they did not directly cause it themselves.

The French president, who leaves office next spring, has faced more than a month of protests in which high-school students have blockaded schools demanding a response to teacher absences, repairs to decrepit buildings and changes to the university applications platform.

Trade unions and gilets jaunes (yellow vest) anti-government protesters are now joining sustained street demonstrations in a growing social crisis over schools, as well as the cost of living and public services. Authorities have increased security measures and placed restrictions on demonstrating after France saw one of its worst days of violence in years earlier this month when largely peaceful demonstrations were marred by looting, fires and vandalism of state buildings.

The senate will this week debate the government’s proposed “vandals pay” law. The legislation would mean that a person protesting could be held liable to pay up to €10,000 for damage and vandalism even if they did not directly cause it themselves, if they were continuing to demonstrate nearby or as part of the same group as perpetrators. The bill also provides for greater use of drones over protests.

The prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, said the bill, which was originally prepared in the wake of violent clashes after Paris Saint-Germain’s victory over Arsenal in the football Champions League in May, was “absolutely essential” after looting and burning during recent demonstrations across France.

The bill comes as the government struggles to contain the current crisis. Marine Le Pen, of the far-right, anti-immigration National Rally (RN), has seen her frontrunner status in next spring’s presidential election boosted as she seeks to reinforce her law-and-order credentials and back police.

Le Pen, who has lodged an appeal to France’s highest court over her conviction for embezzlement of European parliament funds, launched her presidential campaign on Sunday at a rally in Orléans, promising to “bring back order to France”.

The RN has claimed the “vandals pay” bill was originally its idea and Le Pen said she would ensure damage to property was paid for by rioters. Le Pen told a cheering crowd of more than 8,000 people at the rally: “Vandals will pay and if it takes their whole life to pay, then they will spend their whole life paying.”

She said: “We are going to restore the rule of law. Who can claim that there is rule of law when hordes come to ransack and burn our buildings?”

Éric Coquerel, from Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s radical left La France Insoumise, said on Sunday that the “vandals pay” law “would mean the end of street demonstrations” in France because people would not want to take the risk of being held responsible and made to pay up to €10,000 for vandalism they had not committed. The Communist senator Fabien Gay told the parliamentary TV channel Public Sénat: “No demonstration could take place again in our country.”

In an open letter to Le Monde, leftwing trade unions and France’s Human Rights League wrote: “This unfair law, which is a serious attack on the freedom to demonstrate, should be abandoned, or risk a major step back for the rule of law.”

At this weekend’s protests there was widespread anger at Macron for banning non-union demonstrations that his government deemed “illegitimate” and for keeping all protesters away from city centres.

Although Macron has not put in place a state of emergency, the government and local authorities have introduced limits on demonstrating, including bans on gatherings in front of schools and demonstrating in city centres, as well as curfews in some places and extended periods of police custody for the record number of people arrested.

At demonstrations this weekend, many said they had come out to defend the French right to protest in the street. Street protests in France, which are seen as a fundamental way for people to make themselves heard by a centralised state, have regularly been used to express criticism of changes to the law, from pension changes to same-sex marriage.

Serge Slama, a professor of public law at Université Grenoble Alpes, told Telerama magazine: “Although a state of emergency has been ruled out [by Emmanuel Macron] at this point, we have seen a number of decrees bringing a wide restriction on public liberties.”

He said this was “unprecedented” and would benefit the far right if they won elections next year, allowing them to put in place further crackdowns without changing the law.

Lecornu will meet representatives of protesting high-schoolers on Monday as the government comes under pressure to respond to their demands with funding and school repairs in order to avoid further school blockades.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.title: NFL roundup: Falcons spoil Niners’ undefeated start; Steelers win in Paris
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.author: Agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.text:
Michael Penix Jr threw three touchdown passes, Atlanta scored 13 points off four turnovers and the Falcons handed the San Francisco 49ers their first loss, 29-20. San Francisco were already thin at wide receiver before its offense faced additional limitations when running back Christian McCaffrey missed much of the first half with a thigh injury. Brock Purdy threw two interceptions, one of them by rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels. Daniels also recovered a fumble by George Kittle. Penix threw scoring passes to Nick Muse, Kyle Pitts and Drake London as the Falcons snapped a two-game skid.

Harrison Smith capped another dominant performance by Minnesota’s defense with the game-sealing interception, and the Vikings overcame another sluggish start to stay unbeaten with a 16-10 victory over the spiraling Indianapolis Colts. Linebacker Blake Cashman led the onslaught of pressure on Daniel Jones all afternoon with 12 tackles, two sacks, four passes defensed and three quarterback hits as the Vikings improved to 6-0 despite minimal production from the offense. The Colts fell to 2-5. Jones went 13 for 122 for 108 yards and lost 44 yards on four sacks, and Spencer Shrader missed two field goals in the second half.

Malik Willis lead the Miami Dolphins to their first win of the season with a 28-25 victory over the New York Jets. It was the first win for Jeff Hafley as coach of the Dolphins, who avoided an 0-6 start for the first time since 2019. They scored on their first two drives and controlled most of the game. The Jets are 2-5 and made a late push, but Willis sealed the victory with a first down on fourth-and-1. Willis threw two touchdown passes and ran for a score. Geno Smith threw three touchdown passes and an interception for the Jets.

Aaron Rodgers threw one touchdown pass and Chris Boswell kicked three field goals in Pittsburgh’s 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in the NFL’s first regular-season game in France. Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and scrambled for a key first down late in fourth quarter as the Steelers (5-2) won their third straight game. Linebacker Payton Wilson had a red zone interception of Tyler Shough in the third quarter and the Saints (2-5) couldn’t recover. New Orleans rushed for just 18 yards.

Devin Singletary’s 30-yard touchdown run in overtime lifted the New York Giants to a 27-21 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday. Cam Skattebo had a 16-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter and his 42-yard scamper to set up Singletary’s game-winning run. He had 17 carries for 124 yards after not having a carry last Sunday following a costly fumble two weeks ago. JJ McCarthy moved the ball effectively for the Giants (4-2-1) in his first start of the season after coach John Harbaugh benched Jameis Winston. He was 20 of 28 for 252 yards in the stadium in which he won the national title with Michigan in January 2024. The Texans (2-5) got the ball first in overtime, but New York’s defense forced a three-and-out with Kayvon Thibodeaux dropping a potential interception on second down.

Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes in the second half, and the Cincinnati Bengals rebounded from a desultory first two quarters to beat Baltimore 35-13, handing the Ravens a second straight divisional loss with Lamar Jackson sidelined. Baltimore dominated the first half but led only 13-0 after settling for a couple short field goals. Then the Ravens blew a double-digit second-half lead for the second straight week and 10th time since the start of the 2022 season. Baltimore has outscored opponents by 65 points in the first half this season, while being outscored by 70 in the second.

Deshaun Watson has led his fifth game-winning drive in the fourth quarter this season. He connected with Harold Fannin Jr on a 36-yard catch-and run that set up Andre Szmyt’s 32-yard field goal as time expired, and the Cleveland Browns beat the Tennessee Titans 27-24 on Sunday for their fifth win in six games. Watson ran for a touchdown and threw for 308 yards. Quinshon Judkins ran for 96 yards and two touchdowns, and rookie KC Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards in his best game yet. The Titans were trying to string together back-to-back wins for the first time in nearly four years.

Bucky Irving ran for 106 yards and two touchdowns, and Tampa Bay forced four turnovers as the Buccaneers hammered the Carolina Panthers 43-13 on Sunday in Baker Mayfield’s return. Mayfield had missed the previous three games with a dislocated right thumb. He attempted just 11 passes and threw for 64 yards while wearing a protective glove on his right hand. That was more than enough for him to improve to 7-1 against the Panthers, including 6-1 since joining the Bucs. Mayfield didn’t need to do much because Tampa Bay’s run game, defense and special teams dominated. The Bucs had 258 yards on the ground.

https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.title: ‘Whimsical witch stuff’ and vintage radio shows: how horror novelists celebrate Halloween
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.author: Lauren Gould
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.text:
Four horror novelists – Riley Sager, Leah Rowan, Rachel Harrison and Grady Hendrix – share advice for embracing Halloween, even if you’re a scaredy cat

In October, horror lovers can finally rejoice in the season’s endless supply of spooky films, haunted houses and macabre decor.

Others prefer to bask in the comforting glow of the TV while enjoying their 70th rewatch of Hocus Pocus (which arguably is scarier than you might think).

No matter what camp you fall into, you can still enjoy October, or “spooky season” as millennials call it. So I asked the most qualified people I could think of – horror novelists – how to enjoy the season.

“We don’t need to love Freddy and Jason to love horror. It’s a very broad spectrum,” said Rachel Harrison, bestselling author of the witchy novel Cackle and the haunting read, Play Nice. Riley Sager, author of The Unknown and Home Before Dark, suggests a low-key alternative: spooky vintage radio shows. “They are not terrifying. They’re just chilling,” he said. (His recommendations include Three Keleton Key and Sorry Wrong Number.) They also shared how they celebrate the season and, perhaps most importantly, their favorite Halloween candy.

Looking for a treat rather than a trick? We also recommended the best candy from around the world.

Read the story: Canadian Smarties, Thai sourballs: the best global candies that Americans are missing out on

Rachel Harrison: I love to do a corn maze. I’m very basic in that way. There’s something really special about getting a spiced cider, and I also think it’s funny to just do these wholesome small activities while also writing horror. Give me a Shudder movie marathon, fun-sized Snickers and I’m as happy as can be. Riley Sager: One thing I still do well into my 50s is I carve a jack-o’-lantern; that was such a highlight of Halloween as a child.

Grady Hendrix: As a horror writer, Halloween is a lot of pressure. My Halloween is usually an event. This year I’m boarding up like it’s the zombie apocalypse. I try to have a book and plow through it that night; this year I’m doing The Little Girl Who Lives Down the Lane.

RH: There’s a lot of whimsical witch stuff that you can lean into. There’s horror that’s a little bit cozier and less intense. And so if you want to ease your way into it and sort of say, this is how I can enjoy the season without buying fake blood and eyeballs and going to a haunted house where people jump out at you. And then for films, Lisa Frankenstein is a good spooky season movie that’s not too scary.

GH: For horror fans, a lot of the reason we love horror is we grew up watching horror movies with our friends. [Halloween] is a social time of the year. It’s the only time of the year that isn’t in complete denial about the one thing we have in common, which is that we’re all going to die.

RH: [Kiss Slay Replay] is a horror, time-loop novel that takes place at a fall wedding. I think my books are a good balance of being scary, but also not too heavy. So it’s not bleak … I think horror has a lot of hope in it, and horror can be a lot of fun. I wanted to write a book that felt very cinematic, fun and entertaining.

Leah Rowan: [Marion] is not just a commentary on Psycho; it’s all those slashers.

I worked my way through as an employee at Blockbuster. It’s told as more of a thriller, as a woman who has a lot of rage. It’s kind of cathartic. And, there’s a huge knife on the cover.

RS: It’s (Home Before Dark) haunted houses; it’s family secrets; it’s very spooky. That’s the one that every year this time of year I see the sales tick up.

GH: If there’s one to recommend, it’s The Southern Bookclub Guide to Slaying Vampires.

RH: Most horror writers I know, this is our busy season. I’ve been on the road for two months. Like an accountant is busy in April, we’re busy in October, so I’ve had no time to put up any decorations.

LR: We do a family costume every year; I actually make them myself. (This year, they’ll be dressing up as characters from Disney’s The Little Mermaid)

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Victoria Bekiempis
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Trump again congratulated Ohio senator’s rear end before his cheeky comment about rapper being ‘hard to miss’

Donald Trump reiterated his apparent love for buxom bums during a rally in Michigan on Sunday where he encouraged the crowd to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj’s behind.

Trump’s cheeky comments about Minaj’s derriere came as he explained his recent observation on the Republican Ohio senator Jon Husted’s rear end. Earlier in October, Trump said of the former college football player: “I don’t do this with men very often. I started examining his body, because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass and I looked at the whole – and then I looked at his hands. Look at his hands. He’s got these, like, claws.

Trump was speaking at the rally to support Mike Rogers, the Michigan Republican Senate candidate. The Michigan race between Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed remains neck and neck as both political parties scramble for control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections. But he couldn’t resist his purported other favorite topic.

This afternoon, Trump said the media buzz about these comments was “fake news” neglecting the athletic context of his statements. Trump said he had just learned Husted was a college athlete when he was “looking at him up and down, and I’m studying him”.

Trump insisted his subsequent crack was “in fun”. “I said: I looked at his ass, and I’ve never done that with a man before. It’s true. Off the record, women yes, men no, OK.”

Trump then shouted out Minaj, who the New York Post said was donned in “head-to-toe Gucci” today. Minaj, the paper also reported, was seen walking with Trump after leaving Air Force One.

“By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before – Nicki Minaj,” Trump said, prompting celebratory woos from the crowd. “That’s hard to miss. That – stand up! That’s hard to miss.

“OK, I’m going to get back to my story, Nicki,” Trump continued following still more cheers. “I hope Nicki wasn’t insulted, but we love Nicki. She’s been with us for a long time.”

“I examined his ass,” Trump said of Husted, who was not at the event. “And then I looked at his shoulders. I looked at his feet. I looked at his hand. I looked at his jawline. Studied him. He’s got a jawline.

“I then patted him on the shoulder, and it was like a piece of steel. I’m still recovering,” Trump said.

Trump also recently praised the appearance of Ed Gallrein, theRepublican congressional candidate from Kentucky.

“I needed somebody good, and this guy walks through the door,” Trump remarked of Gallrein, in describing his efforts to find a replacement for anti-Maga incumbent Thomas Massie. “I said, look at this beautiful guy.”

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment about why Trump has been discussing others’ bodies.

Trump’s comments come amid criticism of his language style, which some have likened to grotesquerie.

During a Saturday rally for El-Sayed, Barack Obama joked about Trump’s White House renovation efforts.

“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” the former president said.

Meanwhile, Trump said that the US-Canada trade war would soon be in America’s rear view.

“Canada has been ripping off the US for years. I had to do it,” Trump said of tariffs during the rally. “We’ll have that settled pretty soon. They’re willing to give us anything at this moment.”

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Manchester United board hold crisis talks over Carrick’s future and Howe approach
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Jamie Jackson at Old Trafford
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
Manchester United’s hierarchy are in crisis talks over whether or not to sack Michael Carrick as head coach after he oversaw another torrid defeat, against Bournemouth at Old ­Trafford on Sunday, that left his job in the balance.

Carrick was defiant after the 3-0 humbling, insisting he was not expecting to be removed from his post. “I totally understand the situation,” Carrick said of his job prospects. “I’m not expecting anything in ­particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal and I love this place.”

But the United executive are actively ­considering his dismissal, the ­Guardian understands, with the expectation at the club being that Carrick will be sacked.

Eddie Howe remains the preferred candidate of Jason Wilcox, United’s director of football, should there be a change in the dugout, with the former Newcastle manager’s extensive Premier League experience placing him ahead of other potential ­targets.

Howe would be less expensive to bring in than Unai Emery, another admired candidate, given that Aston Villa would demand about £20m in compensation for the ­Spaniard.

Julian Nagelsmann, the former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by Christopher ­Vivell, United’s head of ­recruitment, but Wilcox’s view may hold more sway with Sir Jim ­Ratcliffe, who ­controls football policy at United. Antonio Conte is another who may be in the frame.

Carrick, who left Bruno Fernandes out of his starting lineup – insisting before kick-off that he did so for football reasons and not because of the captain’s criticism of his ­tactics after the midweek ­Champions League defeat at Como – said: “I’ll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, ­whatever decision is made on anything really. So that’s kind of it. I’m not expecting anything either way.

“It’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know. I will always do my best for the football club and I won’t change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see.”

United endured a sixth defeat in 12 games in all competitions after Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and ­Evanilson scored for Marco Rose’s side. They have won only once in the league this season and sit in 16th. Their last win was on 10 September, against Sabah in the Champions League.

The club cannot announce a sacking until they inform the New York Stock Exchange, which is closed at weekends. When Ruben Amorim was sacked in January, the decision was taken on the Sunday night after the coach’s explosive press conference following a draw at Leeds, but was not announced until the next day.

Carrick made a point of ­applauding the home supporters at the end of the match, pumping his hand to his chest as he walked past a supportive Stretford End. As soon as he disappeared down the tunnel, boos met Fernandes, who was following the manager, alongside other United players.

“It wasn’t a farewell from me,” ­Carrick said. “I’m feeling it for my players, they’re going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment. Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way.

“To have that connection with the supporters, it’s mixed emotions, it’ll take a bit of time to digest but I certainly appreciate their support. The situation is where we are and we haven’t had results or performances that have been good enough.”

On his decision to omit Fernandes, who was an unused substitute, ­Carrick said: “There’s always times when you’re trying to make decisions that are to change the course of play and made a difference, but those are the decisions we made today.”

Harry Maguire, United’s captain in Fernandes’ absence, insisted that the squad were “fully behind” ­Carrick. He said: “Coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season.

As individuals, we’re not ­playing well enough. We have to look at ­ourselves and find something within ourselves to bring more to the team. That’s every player that I’m talking about. When things aren’t going your way you have to do the basics well.”

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.title: Kimi Antonelli storms to US F1 GP victory but is made to wait for title glory
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.author: Giles Richards at the Circuit of the Americas
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.text:
Kimi Antonelli took a dominant victory at the US Grand Prix, with a controlled and composed drive to beat the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc into second place, but it was not quite enough for the Italian to seal his first Formula One world championship at the Circuit of the Americas. The coronation is surely but delayed for a week as Antonelli has made it almost a formality that he will seal the deal at the next round in Mexico.

Antonelli did everything required of him in Austin, taking pole and converting it to a win, his ninth of the season. With his teammate George Russell finishing in eighth place and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton in fourth, the fight is alive but only just, and Antonelli is surely now in position to finish the job next weekend in Mexico City.

Antonelli leads Russell by 123 points and Hamilton by 124. With nine wins the Italian cannot be caught on countback and needs only to be 100 ahead after the Mexican GP. Any finish in front of Russell and Hamilton, or ninth or better regardless of where his two rivals finish, will be enough for the 20-year-old to be the youngest driver to claim the sport’s crown and the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari won in 1953.

In what was something of a stately affair in Austin, enlivened largely by a split strategy with the Mercedes of Antonelli and Russell opting for a one-stop strategy over the two-stopper of Red Bull and Ferrari, the former proved to be the right call. Antonelli led from the off and after putting in a long first stint while his rivals dashed in for new boots, he emerged able to regain the lead and not have to stop again.

The strategy split made the procession at least open to debate for the mid-period until it became clear that the one-stopper was the quicker option. The late phase did see some feisty passing by Max Verstappen who took advantage of his fresher rubber to hustle through the field, as did Leclerc in his wake who was equally brave and ultimately took second place from the Dutchman who finished in third, albeit with the mitigation of some engine-braking problems. Hamilton too made a late pass to claim fourth for Ferrari with Lando Norris in fifth for McLaren.

The race however belonged to Antonelli. He did not put a foot wrong with a cool-headed display as he assuredly put one hand on the title. The Italian went into the weekend insisting he just wanted to have fun, to perform at his best and not let the title play on his mind. He did so with no little success at the Circuit of the Americas, where certainly he was having a good time.

The pole lap, his first since the Belgian Grand Prix in July, had been brilliant, and in the race he demonstrated the same imperious form as when at his very best this season and which has brought him to within touching distance of his record-breaking achievement.

Just as his five-race run of victories at the start of the season had given him command of the title fight, he is closing it out with nerveless control. The pole, he admitted, had been something of a surprise given how strong Red Bull have been of late but the victory was an emphatic reminder that these are the performances Antonelli is always capable of delivering.

Moreover the result will be welcomed with open arms at Mercedes. The minor wobble they experienced when their upgrades brought to Malaysia did not deliver as expected and left the team having to work at bringing the package up to speed looks to be over.

They have addressed it to the extent that its operating window remains narrower but is more workable, and Antonelli looked to be comfortable in the car which was once more enjoying an advantage over the rest of the field.

It is far from the dominance it enjoyed for the first half of the season but what is of most import for Mercedes is that they appear to have successfully addressed it and have confidence on the direction they are taking with the car next season.

On a circuit which represents an all-round test of a car’s strengths, through high-speed corners, slow-speed sections and demanding, heavy-braking zones, a well-balanced ride is essential and the Mercedes once more looked like it was on rails in Antonelli’s hands.

He went into the race in Austin needing to win and he delivered, with a superb drive indicative of the form he has shown across the season, not quite sufficient to clinch it here, but enough to ensure it is all over bar the shouting.

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Sid Lowe at the Camp Nou
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou, and he led them out again with a late, late victory that opens up a whole new world. With three minutes remaining and the energy with which they had played dropping, a wonderful piece of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run on a night in which there were so many of them. Camavinga sprinted into the area, slipped away from Pau Cubarsí and pulled the ball back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish.

It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and Madrid had won it, Mbappé getting his second goal of a special match to end Barcelona’s record nine-game winning run. So much for a battering, so much for Barcelona going nine points clear, the title race run before November; there is life in Madrid and in this league. Life in their manager too; this was planned and executed to perfection, and not the way that might have been expected.
