In one survey, 64% of Israelis questioned said it would not influence their vote, and 17% said it made them less likely to back Netanyahu, against 12% who said it had deepened their resolve to support Netanyahu’s Likud party.

In the closing stages of the closely fought campaign, Netanyahu has also forecast growing financial isolation, saying billions of dollars in annual military aid from the US would dry up soon, and drew a rare public rebuke from the central bank for a repeated claim that Israel could use cryptocurrencies to dodge escalating global sanctions.

“Cryptocurrencies cannot serve as a means to circumvent sanctions,” the Bank of Israel said on Sunday evening. “The right course for the Israeli economy is to maintain economic relations with our primary trading partners and to focus on preventing sanctions and their negative impact on the economy.”

Netanyahu had already laid out a forecast for a bleak, isolated future a year ago, when he said Israel might need to become a militarised “super Sparta”, then rowed back again in the face of fierce criticism from a horrified Israeli public.

His return to this rhetoric and the tactics of fear, particularly after unexpected losses for far-right allies in Serbia and Brazil, raised questions about whether the ultimate political survivor may finally be on the ropes.

Few among his allies or enemies expected his government to survive long after 7 October, much less complete its term. But the majority of polls have been clear for more than two years that his current coalition looks set to lose its slim majority.

https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/o.title: ‘Cocaine is the Gollum of drugs’ – and other things we learned from Anthony LaPaglia’s surprisingly juicy memoir
https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/o.author: Sian Cain
https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/o.text:
The actor opens up about almost playing Tony Soprano, why Quentin Tarantino ‘flipped out’ at him and how he’s ‘pretty much broke’ now

Maybe once a year we get a celebrity memoir that is as good on the juicy stuff – the Hollywood gossip – as the interior excavation; and boy does Anthony LaPaglia deliver both in his new memoir, The Life We Choose. “They say acting is the cheapest form of therapy,” writes the actor, best known for his roles in Without a Trace, Empire Records, Lantana and Frasier. “And that was lucky for me, because, coming up in the way I did, Christ knows I needed it.”

The memoir reveals a lot about his abusive childhood in Adelaide, at the hands of his father, Egidio; and how he went from working as a shoe salesman to moving to the US, to work on Broadway and in Hollywood.

But if you’re after name-drops, there are plenty. LaPaglia is a big fan of: Kiefer Sutherland (who he claims was once trailed by a “70-year-old ex-bov from London named Moe” whose sole job was to make sure Sutherland turned up on set when he was “shitfaced”); Arthur Miller; Allison Janney; Michael Keaton; Stanley Tucci; Mike Myers; the whole cast of Frasier but particularly Kelsey Grammer; Alan Arkin; Kerry Armstrong (“a genius actress and a complete nutcase”); and Hugo Weaving.

LaPaglia has mixed feelings about: Val Kilmer (who he claims once deliberately poured coffee on him); John Landis (“aggressive and condescending”); the Empire Records director, Allan Moyle (the only time LaPaglia walked off a set); his youngest brother, Jonathan LaPaglia (“extremely boring company”); Harvey Weinstein (fair); and his third ex-wife, Alexandra Henkel (whom he won’t even name).

LaPaglia had a tough childhood in the suburb Beefacres (now part of Windsor Gardens) in South Australia. He’s still not a fan of his home town: “There’s a bad energy running through it. Whenever I go back, I feel the same low-frequency unease that used to spook me as a kid … Maybe it was weird for a kid, but even during my school years I worried that if I didn’t one day leave Adelaide, I might never be happy.” Though he credits his childhood for helping him become an actor: “I estimate about 80% of the actors I know sprang from difficult beginnings and had poor relationships with their families … I believe nothing makes an actor better than the deep sense of anger and revenge that often accompanies suffering.”

It wasn’t until 1993, when he was filming So I Married an Axe Murderer in San Francisco, that LaPaglia tried drugs for the first time in his 30s – and really liked them. The memoir includes some incredible lines, including: “Cocaine is the Gollum of drugs. You can go along on it for a while but there is a point where it just grabs you” and “I could buy a sandwich bag half-full of the stuff without putting a dent in my rent or grocery bill”. But he became a “bingeing addict” and went on “a four-day solo bender watching David Attenborough’s greatest hits”. One time, his kitchen drawer started talking to him.

LaPaglia never went to rehab but eventually shook his addiction because he “couldn’t live with the stupidity”. He has dyscalculia and always struggled with numbers, “but for years after I quit drugs, I could remember my dealer’s phone number by heart”.

In 1996, David Chase approached LaPaglia with the pilot for The Sopranos and told him “he had me in mind when he wrote the character of Tony Soprano”. LaPaglia loved the script and tried to convince the former CBS chief executive Les Moonves to take the show on – but while Moonves also loved it, he said it was too racy for network television and that CBS would “gut” what made it great. As “David doggedly persisted and I kept trotting The Sopranos around”, LaPaglia was approved by Arthur Miller himself to play Eddie Carbone in A View from the Bridge on Broadway. “Almost as soon” as he committed to Bridge, HBO picked up The Sopranos – and James Gandolfini was cast as Tony instead.

“James was far and away the best choice to play that part,” LaPaglia writes. “I’d have approached Tony Soprano entirely differently. In fact, David and I already had some disagreements about Tony’s personality and motivation. I wanted to portray a guy who’d escaped the mob only to be sucked back in after the death of his mother. I envisaged a more urbane, very reluctant mafioso.” In a weird coincidence, LaPaglia chose Allison Janney over Edie Falco to play Beatrice Carbone in the Miller production; Falco then went on to play Carmela Soprano, Tony’s wife, on the hit show.

In 2011, LaPaglia was invited to meet Quentin Tarantino to discuss playing an Australian slave trader in Django Unchained. LaPaglia even read with Jamie Foxx for the role. But when production on the film was repeatedly postponed, LaPaglia committed to making Underground, a made-for-TV film directed by his friend – the Australian director Rob Connolly.

“Finally, six months after it was supposed to begin production, Quentin was ready to start filming,” LaPaglia writes – but leaving Connolly’s film would have dashed its chance at funding. “It broke my heart to call [Tarantino] and say I couldn’t do it. The last thing I expected, though, was that he’d flip out: ‘What do you mean you can’t do it?’

“Quentin was genuinely astonished that I would pass on a role in his movie to go and shoot some independent thing for Australian TV. I don’t think he was used to being turned down. ‘Can’t you get out of it?’ he said. ‘Jesus Christ, just get out of it.’” When LaPaglia persisted, he says Tarantino said “I don’t fucking believe this” and hung up on him.

LaPaglia now calls his decision “a classic case of LaPaglia self-sabotage”: Django made $450m (A$646m) worldwide, while Underground was barely seen. “Would I have loved to be in the Tarantino family of actors?” he writes. “Sure, but I also know families can be overrated.” Tarantino ended up playing the Australian slave trader himself, if you’re being generous about the accent.

Tarantino isn’t the only director LaPaglia had a falling out with. He hated working with Landis on the 1992 film Innocent Blood so much that he started having recurring dreams about the director dying violently: “What scared me most was how good I felt when I woke up from them.” While filming he even developed welts all over his body, which mystified his doctor: “I was convinced the hives were a result of intense work-related stress. I was allergic to John Landis.” LaPaglia even almost hit him during a disagreement over a take, but the actor Robert Loggia stopped him: “‘Don’t fucking hit him, kid,’ he breathed in my ear. ‘You’ll never work again if you hit him.’”

Losing control at Landis reminded LaPaglia of his abusive father – so once shooting wrapped, he “booked a flurry of appointments” with his therapist.

While LaPaglia was dating “an up-and-coming young actress” decades ago, she told him “how she literally had to fight off the famed Miramax producer Harvey Weinstein when he tried to maul her in a hotel room”. Months later he met Weinstein at a charity event in Tribeca and confronted him. By LaPaglia’s telling, he called Weinstein a “prick” and told him he knew what he’d done to his girlfriend; Weinstein “smirked” and said, “What are you gonna do about it?”

“I don’t have to do anything about it. It’ll catch up with you sooner or later,” LaPaglia replied, to which Weinstein retorted, “Fuck off … you’ll never work in one of my movies.”

“I never stopped spending like I had an unlimited supply of cash,” LaPaglia writes. Though he once owned houses around the world and had a taste for expensive watches, he now lives in a rented apartment in Santa Monica. “The properties I once owned have all been sold, as have the toys – the vintage motorbikes and the garage full of exotic cars. The only thing of value that remains is one Rolex watch. Other than that, I’m pretty much broke – cleaned out by three divorces and my long-term failure to take direct control of my finances.”

He said after his accountant died in 2024, he had no idea where his money was – until the Internal Revenue Service caught up with him and “I realised how much trouble I was in”. He’s since paid back what he owed – but, he says, “don’t be like me”.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.title: Trump lashes out at Obama for joking that White House looks ‘like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory’ – live
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.author: Robert Mackey (now); Chris Hippensteel, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.text:
Trump defends his renovations and jabs back at his predecessor before boarding plane for rally in Mississippi

Before boarding Air Force One to fly to Mississippi for a campaign rally on Monday, Donald Trump was asked to respond to his predecessor, Barack Obama, joking over the weekend that his renovation of the White House, with “gold everywhere”, has “the White House looking like Saddam Hussein open a Cheesecake Factory.”

While rightwing media outlets have tried to cast Obama’s joke as a jibe at patrons of the restaurant chain – despite a report that his own family frequented the chain during his presidency – Cara Castronuova, a former reality TV fitness trainer now covering the White House for LindellTV, seemed to get confused about the talking point when she asked Trump for comment.

“Do you have a response to Obama,” she asked, “who made fun of the Cheesecake Factory, comparing it to the White House?”

“No,” Trump began before immediately reversing himself with a detailed, 500-word defense of his renovations, woven through with an attack on Obama, the nation’s first Black president, for supposedly being unbothered by “dirt and filth”, channeling a well-known racist trope.

“I’ve taken care of the White House. I fixed it with the finest artisans in the world. We’ve reskinned it. It was in horrible shape,” Trump said, in part.

“Guys like Obama, they would pass the front door, they’d see the broken masonry; they’d see the broken- the beautiful pilasters that were all broken, for years they were broken, and he wouldn’t notice because he doesn’t notice that,” Trump said. “He doesn’t notice dirt and filth that hadn’t been cleaned, where the walls hadn’t been cleaned for years. He doesn’t notice areas that haven’t been painted.”

“So it’s very easy for me to do,” Trump continued. “I do it very very simply because it’s my nature. You know, I’m a very clean person, and the White House was in terrible shape.”

“We have to explain that to Obama because he doesn’t understand it, because he’s not a smart guy,” Trump went on. “We have to explain to Obama that the White House is a symbol of America, and it has to be maintained properly.

“Guys like Obama don’t see it. You don’t see dirt. He doesn’t see filth. He doesn’t see broken ornaments on a building,” Trump added.

The president then turned to the camera to address Obama directly through the lens. “The White House - to president Obama – is a symbol of America. It has to be clean. The columns can’t be broken. The bricks can’t be falling off from under the plaster. And for you to say it’s a Cheesecake Factory, that just shows why you were a lousy president.”

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Justice department charges ex-FBI director James Comey for third time
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Sam Levine
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Comey, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump, accused of leaking information related to US national defense

The justice department charged former FBI director James Comey on Monday with two counts of leaking information related to national defense, the third time the Trump administration has filed criminal charges against one of Donald Trump’s most despised foes.

The charges, filed in federal court in Washington DC, provide few details about what Comey is alleged to have leaked. The government alleges that the former FBI director leaked the information in 2016 and conspired with an unnamed person to give the information to a national news outlet.

Patrick Fitzgerald, Comey’s attorney, said the charges were related to a 5 October 2016 New York Times article that had already been investigated by prosecutors. The case was filed through a criminal maneuver known as an “information” – meaning it was not approved by a grand jury. While prosecutors will eventually have to have the charges approved by a grand jury, filing the charges through an information appears to have been an effort to quickly get the criminal charges in against Comey before the 10-year statute of limitations expires.

“Ten years after the article was published, the government filed an ‘information’ against Mr Comey that was not approved by a judge nor issued by a grand jury. It purports to charge Mr Comey with crimes he did not commit,” Fitzgerald said in a statement.

In a court filing unsealed on Monday, Comey’s lawyers argued the indictment should be dismissed because the statute of limitations had expired and it had been twice investigated and determined no charges should be filed. They also argued that the law required an indictment, not an information, within the 10-year statute of limitations.

Trump fired Comey in 2017 as he worked on an investigation into whether Trump allies colluded with Russia during the 2016 presidential election. The former FBI director has since become an outspoken critic of the president.

Last year, the justice department charged Comey with lying to Congress, but the charges were thrown out after a judge found the prosecutor handling the case, a White House ally installed to bring the case, was unlawfully appointed.

Earlier this year, the justice department filed charges against Comey in federal court in North Carolina for posting a picture of a formation of seashells spelling out “8647” – which for some people is a shorthand way of saying get rid of Trump. Legal experts have said that case is thin.

“Well, they’re back again. It would almost be funny if wasn’t such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice. One that we cannot become numb to,” Comey said in a video posted online.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General, accusing bargain chain of overcharging customers
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Barry Yeoman
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Suit that cites 2025 Guardian investigation alleges ‘pattern of inaccurate pricing’ that ‘affects millions of purchases’

The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states have sued Dollar General, the nation’s largest dollar-store chain, for persistently overcharging customers at its more than 20,000 stores across the United States.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Nashville, cites a Guardian investigation published last December.

“Dollar General has for years engaged in deceptive conduct that harms the very consumers it claims to serve,” said the 95-page legal complaint.

“Although Dollar General promises convenience, low prices, and value, the company has routinely charged customers more at the register than the prices displayed on shelves, price tags, and advertisements. This pattern of inaccurate pricing has persisted for years and affects millions of purchases across the country.”

The lawsuit says the scope of the retail chain’s “pricing misconduct” is “staggering”.

The FTC is the federal agency charged with protecting consumers from deceptive, unfair and anticompetitive business practices. State authorities from Mississippi to Ohio to Nebraska to Utah have joined the case as plaintiffs.

Dollar General did not respond to questions for this story, but has previously said that it was “committed to providing customers with accurate prices on items purchased in our stores”.

The FTC’s allegations are consistent with the Guardian’s December 2025 investigation, which found that Dollar General stores failed more than 4,300 government price-accuracy inspections in 23 states over a three-year period. That article “was the subject of significant internal deliberation and discussions” within the company, the lawsuit said.

The agency noted in the lawsuit that Dollar General has policies in place that are supposed to align register prices with shelf prices. For example, it directs employees to remove and replace outdated labels on certain days of the week. Workers told the Guardian that, because of understaffing, they are often too busy to change those labels.

“Dollar General’s on-paper policies to update pricing achieve little in practice,” the lawsuit said, because “they do not track whether the printed labels are actually affixed to shelves.”

The FTC cited a Guardian interview with a lead sales associate in Louisiana who said: “I threw away tags sometimes, to keep me or a co-worker out of trouble.”

Dollar General told the Guardian in 2025 that it is “disappointed” any time it fails to deliver on its commitment to accurate shelf pricing. In court documents in Ohio, Dollar General’s lawyers have argued that “it is virtually impossible for a retailer to match shelf pricing and scanned pricing 100% of the time for all items. Perfection in this regard is neither plausible nor expected under the law.”

In a statement accompanying the FTC lawsuit, the federal agency noted that Dollar General markets itself as a low-cost alternative to other retailers, and that low- and fixed-income customers rely on the accuracy of its price labels.

“Dollar General has betrayed the trust of millions of American consumers and imposed significant financial harm on communities and consumers who are already struggling to make their paychecks last,” said Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s bureau of consumer protection.

In a separate case, the New York attorney general, Letitia James, announced earlier this month that Dollar General had agreed to a $1.875m deal to settle allegations that it had repeatedly overcharged customers across the state.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Trump administration asks Washington to set aside hundreds of ballots from suspected noncitizen voters
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Associated Press
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
This is the latest sign of the administration’s attempts to challenge states with competitive midterm races that could determine control of Congress

The Trump administration on Monday asked Washington state to set aside any ballots received from more than 400 people it alleges are registered to vote without US citizenship, less than two weeks after making a similar demand in California.

The announcement is the latest sign of the administration’s attempts to sow doubts about the election or its outcome in states with races that will help determine control of the US Senate and House.

In a letter to Washington secretary of state Steve Hobbs, the justice department said it had identified 1,500 votes cast by more than 400 people in prior elections. It asked the state to set aside any ballots they might cast in next month’s midterm elections until state officials can confirm they are legally eligible to vote. The state has more than 5 million registered voters, and the state issues mail ballots to all of them.

At a news conference, Charles Neil Floyd, the acting US attorney in Seattle, said he believed the 405 voters identified so far represented “the tip of the iceberg”.

“Because of limitations the state has placed on our investigation, we’ve only been able to uncover a fraction of the total number,” he said.

Hobbs said he was reviewing the justice department’s request. His office noted that the data shared by the department included the last time each of the 405 people voted. One was in 1994.

“The timing of this request – one week before the general election – is no doubt intended to cast unfounded suspicion on the results,” Hobbs said.

Much of the list was built based on “recent contacts” with suspected noncitizens, Floyd said, because federal officers are now routinely checking to see if the people they interact with are registered to vote.

Without access to those state records, proving someone illegally voted will be difficult, Floyd said. The justice department has demanded information including addresses, dates of birth, driver’s license numbers and partial social security numbers.

The effort is the latest by the administration to identify noncitizen voters, even though noncitizen voting is exceptionally rare. Donald Trump has repeatedly sought to undermine public confidence in elections.

Meanwhile, Washington officials have noted that changes in US Postal Service operations have disenfranchised thousands of legitimate voters.

The Washington request marks the third time this month that the justice department has brought a direct state challenge as voting is under way. All three states – Washington, California and Alaska – have House or Senate races that will help determine the balance of power in the country's Capitol.

The race for Washington’s third congressional district is one of the most competitive in the country in this year’s midterm elections. Democrats are counting on congresswoman Marie Gluesenkamp Perez winning reelection as crucial to their strategy of retaking the majority in the House. She has won twice in a district that also has supported the president each time he’s been on the ballot.

The justice department sued California as part of a similar attempt to require the state to set aside mail ballots from up to 20,000 people the federal government suspects may not be citizens. Another lawsuit filed in Alaska last week seeks to delay certification of the vote if the Republican incumbent doesn’t win.

In California, a panel of federal appellate judges heard rare Sunday arguments and questioned the timing, constitutionality and authority of the Department of Justice’s demand. On Monday, they declined to rule on the expedited timeline the justice department requested and sent it back to a lower court.

The elections clause of the US constitution gives state legislatures the power to set the time, place and manner of congressional elections.

Los Angeles county assistant registrar-recorder Monica Flores said in a court filing that her staff went through a sample of 200 records from the Trump administration’s list. They found the sample included canceled or inactive registrations, people with no voting history and voters who appeared to have been born in the United States.

California state officials touted the appeals court’s decision on Monday as a victory for voting rights. The state’s attorney general Rob Bonta vowed to “fight back against the administration’s unlawful overreach at every turn”. California governor Gavin Newsom meanwhile accused Trump of an assault on democracy.

The justice department told Washington it anticipates sending the state an additional list of people it suspects are not citizens prior to election day. It also noted that some of the people it suspects registered without citizenship may have since become naturalized.

https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.title: Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, to co-host Junior MasterChef Australia: ‘It was an easy yes’
https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.author: Emma Joyce
https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text:
After Meghan appeared on MasterChef Australia this year, co-host Poh Ling Yeow says being reunited with the Duchess on the children’s version ‘will be a real treat’

The Duchess of Sussex is set to co-host Junior MasterChef Australia, the children’s version of the popular televised cooking competition, in 2027.

Meghan made her debut appearance on the adult version of MasterChef Australia in July this year, which was filmed during a four-day visit to Australia with Prince Harry in April. Network 10 said the Duchess’s appearance on the show drew its “largest Sunday audience since 2023”.

Now the broadcaster has confirmed Meghan will co-host Junior MasterChef Australia, the children’s version of the show with contestants aged between nine and 13.

No date has been set for production, which will take place at Melbourne Showgrounds.

“I had an incredible time with the whole team at MasterChef this past April, so when they approached me to come back and work with this young group of talent, it was an easy yes,” the Duchess of Sussex said in a statement.

“I love cooking with my own kids, so seeing what these young stars create in the kitchen is going to be a lot of fun. I can’t wait to see what they cook up!”

It is unknown whether it means a temporary relocation to Australia for Meghan, Prince Harry and their children Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five. The family relocated to the UK in August, after living in California for six years.

Meghan will host Junior MasterChef Australia with current MasterChef Australia judge Poh Ling Yeow, who will continue to judge the adult show in 2027 as well.

“I had a lovely time filming with Meghan earlier this year, and being reunited will be a real treat,” Yeow said in a statement. “I can’t wait to meet our pint-sized culinary adventurers.”

The news of Meghan’s next television appearance comes in the same week the Duchess of Sussex revealed she had been made aware that her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, had been accused of possessing child sexual abuse images.

Meghan’s half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, reported to authorities in the Philippines last week alleging that he had discovered a stash of child sexual abuse images at his father’s former home there.

Markle Sr has denied possessing child sexual abuse images, calling the accusations “sick” and “a bunch of lies”. He claimed the computers had not been in his possession since he left Mexico with his son in 2025.

The allegations against Markle Sr are currently being investigated by a human trafficking and child sexual exploitation taskforce in Cebu, authorities have confirmed.

On Sunday, Meghan revealed in a statement through her spokesperson that the Met had made her aware of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2019.

“I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed,” she said.

The Sussexes are reported to have settled in the Cotswolds after leaving the US. In September, they condemned the “reckless intrusion” of two photographers who were spotted outside Archie and Lilibet’s school. Their children have since moved schools.

The Duchess of Sussex’s lifestyle show With Love, Meghan ran for two seasons on Netflix. It has been widely reported that the show won’t return for a third season despite Netflix reporting it was viewed 5.3m times globally in the first half of 2025.

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Harry Kane claims men’s Ballon d’Or to end England’s 25-year wait for winner
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Barney Ronay at the London Palladium
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
Harry Kane is the Ballon d’Or winner for 2026, the first Englishman to win football’s most prestigious individual trophy in 25 years.

Two hours into a lavishly excitable ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London, Kane’s name emerged from the final envelope to wild cheers inside the auditorium. The women’s Ballon d’Or, awarded moments earlier, was won by Alexia Putellas of London City Lionesses, a third Ballon, five years on from her first in the colours of Barcelona.

In the men’s voting, Kane finished ahead of co-favourites Lamine Yamal of Barcelona and Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid, an outcome that will perhaps cause the familiar consternation among the hierarchy of those clubs, not to mention the vast online fan army attached to the superstar players in Kane’s wake.

But Kane is also a fully deserving winner of football’s ultimate gong. The L’Équipe-sponsored trophy is awarded by a vote of journalists and administrators across the footballing super-scape. For Kane, it is reward for a year during which he has won the European Golden Boot, played a major role in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga title, captained England to a World Cup semi-final, and above all shown himself to be a wonderfully humble superstar player.

“It was really tough this year, the incredible players I was up against,” Kane said as he received the trophy, going on to congratulate everyone else nominated for anything else, and thank pretty much everyone he has ever played with.

“I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special,” he added.

As a pure goalscorer, his numbers are astonishing this year, with 89 goals for club and country since the start of August 2025. At Bayern, Kane has also become a darling of the Bundesliga for his all-round game, creativity, intelligence and professionalism. Bayern paid a record €100m fee up front for Kane three years ago, a transfer that broke the club’s usual recruitment patterns and raised some concerns, given Kane was 30 at the time.

It is a measure of his contribution on and off the pitch that this outlay is now seen as entirely vindicated. As a Ballon d’Or winner, Kane now enters rarefied company, heir to a prize that revolved around the Messi-Ronaldo two-hander for so many years, and which promises not just a form of sporting ultimacy but a vast uplift in current and future commercial earnings.

More widely, the award is a coronational moment for Kane himself, 16 years into a professional career that has taken in loan spells at Leyton Orient and Millwall, running himself into the ground to make it in the Premier League, and now, for posterity, into the lineage of elite footballers.

Earlier this month, Kane equalled England’s all-time caps record, while nudging his international goal tally on to 91 in 125 appearances. Aged 33, he still has a home Euros two years from now in his sights as England’s captain and a final opportunity for a different kind of footballing immortality.

https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/o.title: Jay-Z to headline 2027 Super Bowl half-time show
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/o.author: Sian Cain and agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/o.text:
Rapper who has helped produce the Super Bowl show for years is stepping up to perform himself, at SoFi Stadium in California

After years of producing the Super Bowl half-time show, Jay-Z has announced that the 2027 headline act will be none other than himself.

After days of speculation, the NFL, Apple Music and Jay-Z’s company Roc Nation announced on Monday night that the rapper will be the featured performer for the half-time festivities at the Super Bowl LXI on 14 February at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

“From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” said the 56-year-old rapper in a statement. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to advise on and help produce the league’s entertainment presentations, including the Super Bowl half-time show, beginning with Shakira and Jennifer Lopez’s performance at Super Bowl LIV in 2020.

At the time, Jay-Z said he had told the NFL commissioner, Roger Goodell, “If this is about me performing at the Super Bowl, then we can just end this conversation now.”

“When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him,” he said. “I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”

Monday’s announcement came a week after reports first emerged that Jay-Z would perform, with some observers speculating that it was unlikely due to his lack of recent hits. Jay-Z’s last solo album, 4:44, was released in 2017 while his last collaborative album was made with his wife, Beyoncé, in 2018, performing together as the Carters.

He just closed his Jay-Z 30 concert tour over the weekend at the SoFi Stadium, after performing several dates in New York and London.

Born Shawn Carter, Jay-Z has won 25 Grammy awards and received 89 nominations, the second-most in history behind his wife, who has performed at two Super Bowls. His catalogue includes the albums Reasonable Doubt, The Blueprint and The Black Album, and hit songs such as Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem), 99 Problems and Empire State of Mind, his collaboration with Alicia Keys.

His 1996 debut, Reasonable Doubt, was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame last year.

Jay-Z’s career has extended into music publishing, artist management and sports. He co-founded Roc-A-Fella Records and founded Roc Nation in 2008, building it into an entertainment company that works with artists and athletes.

Jay-Z became the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2017 and joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021.

Bad Bunny performed at last season’s Super Bowl in February, bringing on special guests including Lady Gaga, Ricky Martin, Jessica Alba, Karol G, Cardi B, Young Miko, and Pedro Pascal.

The Puerto Rican superstar’s songs had sharp gains across streaming charts, playlists and music discovery platforms in the hours after the show.

Past Super Bowl half-time show headliners include Kendrick Lamar, Rihanna, the Weeknd, Michael Jackson, the Who, Madonna, Coldplay and the Blues Brothers.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.title: Golden State Valkyries one win from WNBA title after Game 5 win over Atlanta Dream
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.author: Associated Press
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.text:
Kiah Stokes had 13 points, eight rebounds and three blocked shots as the Golden State Valkyries moved within one win of a championship in their second season, beating the Atlanta Dream 64-55 in Game 5 of the WNBA finals on Monday night.

Angel Reese finished with seven points, 15 rebounds and five assists – a big difference from her two standout performances in the first two games of the series at Chase Center. Reese shook her head when whistled for the second of her three offensive fouls with 7:43 to play.

Fans screamed and clapped thunder sticks following the final buzzer as Stokes spoke from the floor to chants of “MVP!”

In the US, the series will air on NBC, USA Network and CNBC, with all games streaming on Peacock. In the UK, it will be carried by Sky Sports. In Australia, fans can watch through WNBA League Pass, with selected coverage also available through ESPN.

On a night leading scorer Gabby Williams struggled to find her shooting touch, Golden State found the “strength in numbers” mantra coach Natalie Nakase has praised all season long. Veronica Burton had 13 points and eight rebounds.

On Saturday, Nakase had changed up her lineup for a 67-62 Game 4 win by inserting Tiffany Hayes and Kaila Charles into the starting five. She stayed with those two Monday night, and it worked again. Hayes, who played 10 seasons for Atlanta and came out of retirement two years ago, had 12 points – and Nakase has said she wants to win it all for the veteran guard.

Williams began 2 for 11 and missed all four of her three three-point tries, but she converted a three-point play with 9:08 remaining put the Valkyries ahead 49-42 and finished with nine points on 3-for-14 shooting and six rebounds.

Atlanta will now try to stave off elimination at home on Thursday in Game 6 and force a deciding Game 7 back at Chase Center on Saturday. The Dream hurt themselves with 17 turnovers that led to 21 points for Golden State.

Stokes hit a key three-pointer with 2:46 to go in the third quarter and another with 7:21 left in the game, which ignited chants of “Ki-ah! Ki-ah!” from the fervent “Ballhalla” home crowd.

Golden State owner Joe Lacob promised a championship within five years when the expansion franchise was granted to the Bay Area three years ago, yet this season has exceeded even what he could have envisioned.

Earlier Monday, the league announced Game 6 would be played at 17,000-seat State Farm Arena in Atlanta starting at 12.30pm EDT on Thursday – a time when many fans on both coasts will be working.

“I’d like to see it be a national holiday for all WNBA championship games so whatever somebody can do,” Dream coach Karl Smesko said. “I hope everybody gets to see it somehow and I know that for some people it’s not realistic, they have jobs and won’t be able to make it. So I’m disappointed for that but I’m really hopeful that as many people can see the game as possible.”

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.title: Ruthless Brewers close in on World Series sweep after crushing Rays 10-1 in Game 3
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.author: Associated Press
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o.text:
Jackson Chourio and Brice Turang sparked Milwaukee’s eight-run fifth inning, and the Brewers routed the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 on Monday night to move within one victory of their first World Series title.

Rookie left-hander Robert Gasser pitched one-hit ball and faced the minimum through six innings as Milwaukee rolled to a 3-0 lead in the World Series. Game 4 is Tuesday night at Tropicana Field, where many Brewers fans showed up Monday and cheered from behind the visitors’ dugout.

Gasser allowed a line-drive single to Yandy Díaz leading off the bottom of the first and then retired 14 straight before Victor Mesa Jr walked to start the Tampa Bay sixth. With the help of a caught stealing and a double play, Gasser became the first starter to face the minimum 18 batters through six innings of a World Series game since Arizona’s Curt Schilling in 2001 – and the first left-hander to do it since Sandy Koufax for the Los Angeles Dodgers in 1965.

Fri 23 Oct Game 1: Milwaukee 3, Tampa Bay 2Sat 24 Oct Game 2: Milwaukee 5, Tampa Bay 4Mon 26 Oct Game 3: Milwaukee 10, Tampa Bay 1Tue 27 Oct Game 4: Milwaukee at Tampa Bay, 8pm (Fox)Wed 28 Oct Game 5: Milwaukee at Tampa Bay, 8pm* (Fox)Fri 30 Oct Game 6: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm* (Fox)Sat 31 Oct Game 7: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm* (Fox)

In the US, all World Series games will air on Fox and Fox Deportes, with streaming available through Fox One. In the UK, the series will be carried by TNT Sports. In Australia, fans can watch on ESPN, with streaming available through Disney+ and Kayo Sports.

Chourio went 4-for-5, William Contreras was 3-for-5 and Milwaukee racked up 16 hits off “Fastball Freddy” Peralta and five relievers to win their eighth straight postseason game and fourth in a row on the road.

Of the 43 previous major league teams to fall behind 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, only the 2004 Boston Red Sox rallied to win four straight when they beat the New York Yankees in the American League Championship Series.

Gasser became the first starter for Milwaukee to get an out in the sixth inning this postseason. He has allowed one run in 15 innings over three starts, all on the road.

Peralta, the MVP of the ALCS against Cleveland, ran out of gas against the Brewers. He was charged with five runs and seven hits in four and two-thirds innings against his former team.

After a pair of tense, down-to-the-final-pitch, one-run games in Milwaukee, the Brewers put this one out of reach in the fifth with a postseason-record seven straight hits with two outs.

Chourio began the rally with a one-out single and then stole second with two outs. Christian Yelich walked, and Peralta exited after Contreras’ infield single loaded the bases.

The inning appeared to end when third baseman Junior Caminero fielded Contreras’ bouncer and threw to second base for a forceout. But the call at second was overturned after a replay review, and Cam Booser entered.

Turang ripped a liner that shortstop Taylor Walls couldn’t short-hop. It bounced off his glove and rolled into shallow center, allowing two runs to score.

Garrett Mitchell followed with an RBI single, Cooper Pratt grounded a two-run double down the left-field line and Sal Frelick lined a run-scoring double to make it 8-0.

Cole Sulser replaced Booser and allowed an RBI single to David Hamilton and an RBI double to Chourio, who became the second-youngest player with four hits and a stolen base in a World Series game behind Ty Cobb in 1908.

Of the 25 previous teams who took a 3-0 lead in the World Series, 21 swept and four won in five games.

Originally the Seattle Pilots for one season in 1969, the franchise moved to Milwaukee and was renamed the Brewers in 1970. Their only other trip to the World Series came as an AL team and ended with a loss to St Louis in Game 7 in 1982.

Led by 67-year-old manager Pat Murphy, the Brewers need just one more win to finally end their championship drought.

The Rays led the AL with 98 wins in the regular season, swept the Yankees in three games in the ALDS and beat the Guardians in six games in the ALCS.

But they made uncharacteristic mistakes on the bases and defensively in the first two games, and completely unraveled at home.

Tampa Bay also have never won a World Series in 29 seasons. The Rays lost to the Phillies in five games in 2008 and to the Dodgers in six games in 2020.

Wearing their white Devil Rays uniforms, they were eager to play in front of their home fans at the quirky, cavernous Trop, which had its roof shredded by Hurricane Milton in October 2024 and needed major renovations.

But their cowbell-ringing, towel-waving fans among a sellout crowd of 40,388 couldn’t lift them past the surging Brewers.

The Brewers led the majors with 103 wins, beat the Padres in four games in the NLDS and swept the Dodgers in the NLCS. With a win in Game 4, they would become the first team to sweep an LCS and World Series since the 1976 Cincinnati Reds.
